inputs.coverage_rule: expected_runs = configurations with any saved run x videos in the split directory

solve_budget.reaches_budget: estimate: solve_ilp time >= budget, since termination status is not logged. A time-limited solve cannot read below the budget, so percent is an upper bound. solve_ilp also includes solution readout and cleanup, so an optimal solve can read just above the budget; the runs_* counts bin solve time in multiples of the budget, lower_bound_percent counts solve >= 1.1 x budget (a lower bound if readout and cleanup take at most 0.1 x budget), and median_solve_over_budget >= 1 means the median is set by the budget
solve_budget.rule: p022 passes `time_limit or 0.1` to solve_ilp; a null or zero time_limit used the default

source: <cache>/<dataset>/execution/<video>/022_pruned_polyominoes/<param>/score/runtime.jsonl, every saved run (one clip under one pruning configuration)

timing_boundaries.build_ms: Gurobi environment creation and start, model creation, and constraint construction
timing_boundaries.clip_position: launch_first_clip: first clip of the first 20 tasks a p022 invocation starts (ranked by first write, 1 s resolution, ties share a rank), whose processes start Gurobi at the same moment; other_first_clip: first clip of any other task; later_clip: the rest. A first clip is the first video of the split directory listing, as p022 sorts it. An invocation is a run of writes with no gap over 600 s
timing_boundaries.load: p022 runs 20 tasks (processes) at once and leaves Gurobi Threads at its default, so these are timings under that concurrency, the same logs the throughput numbers sum
timing_boundaries.solve_ms: GRBoptimize, solution readout, and freeing the model and environment
timing_boundaries.stage_ms: all p022 operations: prepare_bitmaps, group_tiles, build_ilp, solve_ilp, extract_grids
